White wisteria claiming the entire front facade, its ivory racemes hanging in dense ropes past the windowsills, the gnarled central trunk pressed flat against the stone like a second wall.
Crimson climbing roses swallowing the chimney stack completely, canes spiraling upward and blooming at the very cap, a few long runners spilling back down across the roofline.
Lavender wisteria draped over the roof ridge like a living thatch, its racemes hanging equally on both slopes, the perfume so thick it seems to thicken the morning air around the eaves.
Deep-violet clematis curtaining the largest window, blooms pressing against the glass in overlapping layers, tendrils threading through the latch hardware and along the stone sill in both directions.
Blush-pink climbing roses framing the front door in an unbroken arch, petals drifting inward across the threshold, canes climbing to the transom and spilling sideways along the facade.
Trumpet vine consuming one full gable end, its scarlet-orange funnels blazing against the pale limewash, thick woody stems splitting at the roofline and reaching fingers across the ridge tiles.
Honeysuckle cascading from the eave of the porch in a fragrant yellow-and-cream waterfall, stems looping through the porch posts and trailing loose tendrils across the flagstone below.
Magenta clematis pouring over the garden-side gable, its large flat blooms overlapping like fish scales across the roof slope, a few hairline tendrils curling onto the neighboring window shutter.
White climbing roses engulfing the east-facing wall, canes fanning outward from a single ancient root, blooms densest at the upper storey where they press into the overhang of the eaves.
Morning glory smothering the porch trellis and spilling onto the roof edge, its violet trumpets open wide in the early light, heart-shaped leaves shingling every horizontal surface.
Jasmine threading up and over the entire door surround, white star-blooms clustered so thickly the lintel disappears, long whip stems reaching upward to lace themselves into the gutter bracket.
Emerald moss and soft shield-ferns sheathing the north roof slope in unbroken green velvet, tiny white toadflax starring the mortar joints, the chimney buried to its flaunching in cushioned growth.
Ivy threaded throughout with tiny white bloom cascading from the roof parapet down the full height of the rear wall, a slow green tide that swallows every course of stone uniformly.
Hops clothing the south wall from ground to eave, their papery green cones hanging in swaying clusters, bine stems twisting upward with such purpose the wall seems to be climbing with them.
Autumn-tinted grape vine draping the pergola attached to the cottage side, amber and burgundy leaves overlapping in deep shadow, heavy clusters of dark fruit hanging at eye level through the posts.

Flowering quince spreading across the lower half of the front facade, its coral-scarlet blossoms appearing directly from the dark stems against the pale stone, branches fanning wide in a flat espalier.
White clematis cascading off the roof edge in a long unbroken veil, its small four-petaled flowers moving in the lightest breeze, the gutter entirely hidden beneath the trailing curtain of stems.
Crimson roses swallowing the garden gate and continuing unbroken up the cottage wall beside it, blooms densest where wall meets gate post, the arch between them almost fully sealed with petals.
Lavender wisteria coiling down a single chimney stack, its racemes hanging the full length of the flue and pooling in loose drapes across the roof lead, the brickwork invisible beneath.

Honeysuckle engulfing a dormer window, stems crossing and recrossing the frame until the wood is entirely sheathed, cream and gold flowers spilling inward across the sill and scenting the room beyond.
Morning glory curtaining the cottage's side window in a sheet of violet bloom, each flower a wide trumpet aimed outward, the sash itself a pale ghost visible only at midday through the growth.

Blush roses colonizing the roof ridge, long arching canes having climbed the chimney and then sprawled horizontally along the apex, petals loosening in the wind and drifting to both sides of the slope.
White jasmine consuming the back-door lean-to entirely, its roof invisible under overlapping starred clusters, stems hanging in loose loops between the corrugated edge and the garden wall behind.
Moss and button-fern carpeting the shaded west gable from ground to eave in layered green plush, every crack in the pointing softened, a single hart's-tongue fern arching from above the lintel.

Grape vine covering the cottage's broad side wall in a tapestry of russet and gold, the wood of the main trunk thick as a wrist where it leaves the soil, leaf shadows moving across the roof slope all afternoon.
